content.thinking:
The key design question for the retry is what happens when a user clicks Retry while a retry is already in flight. The loadAttachments guard lets a request through when the entry is known but failed, so a second click would fire a duplicate request. I need some kind of retrying state in ReaderView to prevent that.

I'm adding a retrying set in ReaderView so a second Retry click gets ignored while a request is already running. The same guard should also stop a revisit from overlapping with an active retry, so I'm thinking about tracking in-flight keys inside loadAttachments.

I'm weighing whether the in-flight check belongs in loadAttachments as a shared set of keys rather than just a retry-specific flag, since that would also block overlapping revisits. Then I'm working out where focus should go after a successful retry, and I'm leaning toward having MessageAttachments track whether its own Retry button started the request.

I'm checking whether focus sits on the Retry button when the note gets replaced, since removing that button would drop focus to the body. On success I want focus on the group container, and I'm checking that MessageAttachments stays mounted through a failed-to-ready transition so this logic can run.

I'm checking whether the mouse case breaks the focus fix, since WebKit and Safari don't focus a button on click, so activeElement might not be the retry button at that point.

I'm weighing whether focus should move to the group only if it was inside the retry button before the swap, or whenever the click came from the mouse, since WebKit and Safari don't focus buttons on click. A test that focuses the button first would cover the keyboard path, and checking for body focus might handle the mouse path without stealing focus from elsewhere.

I'm deciding whether focus should move to the group only when it was inside the retry button before the swap, and I'm settling on that narrower rule so focus never gets pulled away from wherever the user has moved it. Clicks in WebKit and Safari don't focus buttons, so in that case there's nothing to rescue. I'm also checking whether the reader's global key handlers behave differently when focus lands on the group container, though that looks fine as is.

I'm checking the focus ring for the group container, since programmatic focus on a div might need an explicit `:focus-visible` style that matches the house lavender ring, and I'm looking at whether a global focus rule already covers it. I also need to decide how the retry button's label should read while the request is in flight.

I'm settling on the retry button's appearance during the request: it stays mounted, marked aria-disabled, and reads "Retrying…" with a matching accessible name. I'm also checking that the disabled-looking style applies through the aria-disabled attribute, since the default disabled opacity won't cover it.

I'm checking the global button styles and any focus-visible rules, since the aria-disabled retry button needs its own dimmed look and the group focus ring should match the house style.

content.text:
**Status:** complete. Items (a) to (f) are done, with a failing test first for each. Nothing could be rendered on this VM, so every contrast, geometry and focus-ring claim below is computed from tokens and CSS, not sampled.

## Per item

**(a) Composer field underline**
- At rest, `.field-row .field-input` now uses `border-bottom-color: var(--icon-muted)`. On hover the full border is Graphite too. Focus-visible is unchanged: Dusk Lavender plus the inner ring.
- The body `.field-textarea` had the same weak boundary: the global field style gives it `border: 1px solid var(--divider)`, and its fill equals the card fill, so the border was its only cue. It is a composer-only class used only in DraftEditorCore, so I gave it `border-color: var(--icon-muted)`.
- That rule would have beaten the global `:focus-visible` border colour (equal specificity, later in the file). I added `.field-textarea:focus-visible { border-color: var(--focus-accent) }` and test the order.
- The other composer inputs: ReplyComposer and ComposeCard have no inputs of their own. Every field comes from DraftEditorCore, so nothing else needed changing.
- Contrast, computed with a WCAG luminance script (also in the test helper):

| Colour on surface | Ratio |
|---|---|
| Graphite on Lifted Charcoal (#33312e) | 3.79 |
| Graphite on Deep Umber (#1f1e1c, drafts drawer) | 4.87 |
| Seam on Lifted Charcoal | 1.36 |
| Seam on Deep Umber | 1.75 |

  Graphite clears the 3:1 floor on the drawer surface, as you asked me to confirm. Seam fails on both, which the test also asserts.
- I added a comment in the CSS and a DESIGN.md exception. The Don't rule and the Graphite colour entry now name the narrow exception for field boundaries.

**(b) Caveat toggle**
- `.composer-caveat-toggle` now has `padding: 5px; margin: -3px`. The hit area is 14 + 10 = 24px, and the layout box stays 18px, so `.composer-top` does not grow.
- No DraftEditorCore change. The `aria-label` and `aria-expanded` are untouched.
- The test reads the 14px glyph size from the SVG in DraftEditorCore.

**(c) Participants** (`ReaderView.vue`, `style.css`)
- Each participant now has `role="group"` and `aria-label` of `Name, mailbox`, or just the mailbox when there is no name or the name equals the mailbox. The visible `Name <mailbox>` text sits in an inner `aria-hidden` span.
- A bare group takes no name from its content, so without a label it would be announced as just "group". The hidden span stops the address being read twice.
- `tabindex=0`, the hover/focus handlers and the `contactOverride` behaviour are unchanged. Hover and focus context tests pass.
- `.participant:focus-visible` now has a 2px Dusk Lavender outline, 1px offset, 4px radius.
- The claim that participants are only reachable inside an opened Details holds in the DOM. A test confirms the participants are never inside the `summary`, and that none is tabbable while the details is closed. A helper models the browser rule that closed or hidden details content is not focusable. jsdom cannot prove the real browser rule, so that part is a model.

**(d) AttachmentChooser**
- The file button now reads `Save` with `aria-label="Save {displayFileName(file.filename)}"`. The disabled logic is unchanged.
- The tests moved to `Save`. A new test covers the label, including a bidi-control filename. `displayFileName` strips only bidi controls, not path parts, so `../../evil.html` stays as typed, same as the inline list.
- DESIGN.md and `docs/ux-12-safe-attachments.md` are updated. I kept the 2026-11-07 native-evidence line as history and annotated it ("labelled `Save to Downloads` at capture time; since renamed `Save`") instead of rewriting it. The success line is unchanged.

**(e) Retry for file details** (`MessageAttachments.vue`, `ReaderView.vue`)
- A `Retry` button now sits next to the failure note, with `data-test="attachments-retry"` and `aria-label="Retry loading file details"`. It emits `retry`.
- While retrying, the button stays mounted with `aria-disabled="true"` and reads `Retrying…`. Clicks are ignored while it waits, so there is no double request.
- On success, the group (`tabindex=-1`) takes focus only if focus was inside it before the swap. A `pre`-flush watcher on `loadState` checks this while the button still exists. If you moved focus elsewhere, nothing is stolen, and a test covers that. A failed retry keeps the same state, with focus on the button.
- No new live regions. A test asserts there is no `role=status`, `role=alert` or `aria-live` in the failure state.
- I replaced the `attachmentRequests` and `attachmentSeq` token logic with a reactive in-flight `Set`. With one request per key, the token check could never fire. This also stops a J/K revisit during a retry from sending a second request, which the old guard would have allowed for a failed key.

**(f) Details `▸`**
- Partly wrong, as you suspected. The state is already native: a real `<details>/<summary>` whose `open` follows the toggle, with no ARIA added. A test proves it and passed before any change.
- I added the alt-text form right after the fallback: `content: '▸ ' / '';` and the `▾` equivalent. A CSS contract test asserts both lines exist in order.
- I built the bundle (`vite build`, output outside the repo). The minified CSS keeps both declarations, so nothing drops the fallback. The glyph is unchanged and stays Ash, not Graphite.

## Failing before, passing after
- `tests/polish-affordances.css.test.ts`: 7 failed, 3 passed before the CSS edits. All 10 passed after. The three that passed first were the Seam-under-3:1 documentation, the 14px glyph, and the Ash colour.
- `tests/reader.component.test.ts`, polish block: 1 failed before (participant `role`). The two claim-verification tests (native details, no tabbable participant when closed) already passed.
- `tests/attachments.component.test.ts`: 7 failed after the test edit and before the component change. All 12 passed after.
- Retry tests in `tests/reader.status-quote-attachments.component.test.ts`: 4 failed (no `attachments-retry` element), all passed after.

## Checks
- `npx vitest run` on the focused files: passed throughout.
- `pnpm test`: 67 files passed, 4 skipped. 1087 tests passed, 34 skipped. The skipped files are the four `*.rendered*` tests, which need a browser and could not run here.
- `pnpm typecheck`: clean. It caught one wrong `.get().exists()` in my test, which I fixed.
- `~/.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable detect --json …` on the five components: `[]`.

## What only a render can confirm
- Whether the Graphite underline reads too heavy against the quiet inputs, and the full Graphite box of the body field next to the underlined rows. This is the main judgement call. If it looks heavy, only the textarea's `border-color` line needs reverting.
- The 24px caveat hover chip, whose 3px overlap into neighbouring space is invisible but real.
- The participant ring on wrapped lines, because inline outlines break across lines.
- Screen-reader output for `role="group"` plus `aria-label`, and the empty-alt glyph in WKWebView. Older WebKit may ignore the `/ ''` form, which falls back to the prior behaviour.
- Mouse clicks on macOS WebKit do not focus buttons, so the Retry focus handoff only matters for keyboard use.
- The four `*.rendered*` test files were skipped (they need a browser). I checked by grep that none asserts the changed strings or ARIA, but they did not run.
